title: Analyzing TGF-β Signaling in Colitic Mice Using Flow Cytometry and Western Blotting
author: Fujiwara, Garo, et al.
materials: On the day before the experiment.1.Prepare buffers A, B, and C. Keep at 4°C for up to 2 weeks. For 20 mice, make 1500 mL of Buffer A, 500 mL of Buffer B, and 500 mL of Buffer C.2.Label 100 × 15 mm style petri dishes, sterile 50 mL centrifuge tubes (five tubes per mouse), sterile 25cm2 vented cap, TC treated tissue culture flasks (two per mouse), and 2 mL Eppendorf tubes (one per mouse).3.Place 100 μm cell strainer on one 50 mL conical tube per mouse and a 40 μm cell strainer on one 50 mL conical tube per mouse.

On the day of the experiment, before euthanization.4.Set the incubator shaker at 37°C.5.Add 0.077 g DTT to Buffer C and warm up 10 mL of Buffer C per mouse at 37°C.6.Warm up 10 mL per mouse of the X-VIVO 15 Serum-Free medium with Gentamicin and Phenol Red at 37°C.7.Fill two sets of 50 mL conical tubes with Buffer A and keep them on ice.CRITICAL: Animal work can only be performed after appropriate approval is obtained and under the applicable guidelines and regulations.

steps.title: Prepare buffers and label consumables
steps.instruction: On the day before the experiment, prepare Buffers A (1500 mL), B (500 mL) and C (500 mL) for up to 20 mice, keep them at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks, label 100 × 15 mm petri dishes, five sterile 50 mL tubes per mouse, sterile 25 cm² vented caps, two TC‑treated tissue‑culture flasks per mouse, and one 2 mL Eppendorf tube per mouse; place a 100 µm cell strainer on one 50 mL tube per mouse and a 40 µm strainer on another.

steps.title: Warm buffers and media
steps.instruction: On the day of the experiment, set the incubator shaker to 37 °C; add 0.077 g DTT to Buffer C and warm 10 mL of Buffer C per mouse at 37 °C; warm 10 mL of X‑VIVO 15 serum‑free medium with Gentamicin and Phenol Red per mouse at 37 °C; fill two sets of 50 mL conical tubes with Buffer A and keep them on ice.

steps.title: Dissect colon and collect tissue
steps.instruction: Euthanize mice, dissect the entire colon by incising at the anus and just below the cecum, briefly rinse in 1× PBS, lay flat on a paper towel, wet forceps and squeeze out feces, clean forceps between samples, remove attached fat, cut colon longitudinally and open lumen, transfer each colon into a 50 mL conical tube containing ice‑cold Buffer A, vortex 10 s and keep on ice.

steps.title: Transfer tissue to pre‑warmed Buffer C
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL of pre‑warmed Buffer C containing DTT to a 25 cm² flask (one per colon), place a metal tea strainer on a large beaker, vortex each 50 mL tube with colon tissue in Buffer A, pour over the strainer to remove buffer, pat the tissue dry on a paper towel, then transfer the colon tissue to the flask containing 7.5 mL pre‑warmed Buffer C with DTT; close flasks, seal caps with parafilm.

steps.title: First enzymatic digestion
steps.instruction: Place sealed flasks horizontally in a 37 °C incubating shaker, secure with tape, incubate 20 min at 180 rpm (add 5 min if incubator not pre‑warmed); meanwhile thaw Liberase and DNase I aliquots at 37 °C and prepare 10 mL enzyme solution per mouse, keep the enzyme solution at 37 °C.

steps.title: Stop first digestion and prepare second
steps.instruction: After 20 min, place flasks on ice, transfer each colon tissue to a new 50 mL tube with 10 mL ice‑cold Buffer A, vortex briefly, pour over a tea strainer, move tissue to a 2 mL Eppendorf tube, chop with clean scissors for 1.5 min (wipe scissors between samples), add 900 µL cold Buffer B, dip scissors to collect remaining pieces, keep on ice; spin tubes at 2 800 × g for 1 min at 4 °C, carefully remove supernatant and floating fat, resuspend pellet with 1 mL pre‑warmed enzyme solution, vortex, pour into a new 7.5 mL flask; repeat resuspension two more times for a total of 3 mL enzyme solution, then add 7 mL more enzyme solution to reach 10 mL per tissue, close caps, seal with parafilm, place flasks horizontally in the shaker and incubate 40 min at 120 rpm, 37 °C.

steps.title: Prepare ice‑cold Buffer A for final wash
steps.instruction: During the last 5 min of the 40‑min incubation, add 10 mL ice‑cold Buffer A into a separate 50 mL tube fitted with a 100 µm cell strainer and keep on ice.

steps.title: Harvest and filter digested cells
steps.instruction: Immediately after incubation, place flasks on ice, transfer the suspension to a 10 mL pipette and pass through the prepared 100 µm strainer tube, wash each flask with 10 mL ice‑cold Buffer A and pass the wash through the same strainer, mash tissue through the strainer with a 1 mL syringe plunger, discard any remaining white membranous tissue, add another 10 mL ice‑cold Buffer A to each strainer and discard the strainer, return the flow‑through to the 50 mL tube, spin at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 10 mL ice‑cold Buffer A, pipet up/down and transfer the suspension over a 50 mL tube fitted with a 40 µm strainer, wash the 40 µm strainer with 10 mL ice‑cold Buffer A, bring the final volume to 30 mL with ice‑cold Buffer A, spin again at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant and keep the pellet for downstream antibody staining and cell sorting.

steps.title: Intracellular phospho‑Smad2/3 staining
steps.instruction: Transfer the cell pellet to a 96‑well round‑bottom plate, centrifuge 5 min at 420 × g and discard supernatant; resuspend cells in 100 µL 1× fixable LIVE/DEAD (Zombie Aqua) stain prepared by diluting 1 µL dye in 1 mL PBS, incubate 10 min at 37 °C; wash with 100 µL PBS, centrifuge 5 min at 420 × g, discard supernatant; fix in 100 µL 2 % PFA in PBS, incubate 10 min at 37 °C, centrifuge 5 min at 420 × g, discard; permeabilize with 100 µL ice‑cold methanol, incubate 60 min at 4 °C in the dark; wash twice with 200 µL FACS buffer (centrifuge 5 min at 420 × g each), then incubate with 100 µL FACS buffer containing 2 µL phospho‑Smad2/3 antibody for 60 min at room temperature; wash 100 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge 5 min at 420 × g, discard; wash again with 200 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge 5 min at 420 × g; finally resuspend cells in 200 µL FACS buffer, transfer to flow‑cytometer tubes and store at 4 °C until acquisition.

steps.title: Prepare lysates for western blot
steps.instruction: Collect FACS‑sorted DCs or CD4⁺ T cells (or cells after TGF‑β treatment) in a tube, centrifuge 1 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, keep samples on ice (protein degradation is maximal at room temperature) and optionally store pellets at –80 °C; wash pellet with PBS, remove supernatant, add 200 µL RIPA lysis buffer containing 1× complete mini protease inhibitor cocktail per 10⁶ cells, incubate on ice 1 h with vortexing every 15 min, pass lysate through a bent 27‑gauge needle 10 times, sonicate on ice for 10 cycles at 40 % amplitude (1 s pulse, 10 s off), centrifuge 20 000 × g for 30 min, collect supernatant as whole‑cell lysate; determine protein concentration with Bradford assay, dilute lysates to 5 µg/µL with RIPA, keep aliquots at –80 °C; for SDS‑PAGE, take 30–50 µg protein, add 6× loading buffer to a final volume of 10 µL, heat 100 °C for 10 min, place on ice, centrifuge 7 000 × g for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE and transfer
steps.instruction: Load 10 µL of each protein sample and 10 µL pre‑stained protein standard onto a 4–20 % gradient SDS‑PAGE gel, run at 100 V until the markers separate; briefly immerse a PVDF membrane in methanol (20 s) during the run, then incubate the membrane in transfer buffer; soak blotting papers in transfer buffer for ≥10 min, place the gel in transfer buffer and rock gently 5–10 min; assemble the wet transfer sandwich (PVDF membrane, gel, blotting papers), remove bubbles with a roller, and transfer proteins at 300 mA for 60 min using a wet transfer apparatus.

steps.title: Block and incubate primary antibodies
steps.instruction: After transfer, wash the PVDF membrane twice with TBST (0.1 % Tween‑20); block for 60 min at room temperature on a rocker in 5 % non‑fat milk in TBST; incubate overnight at 4 °C with primary antibody diluted in 5 % milk/TBST: Smad7 (1:500), GAPDH (1:5 000) or α‑tubulin (1:5 000); following incubation, rinse twice with PBST, then wash three times with TBST for 10 min each at room temperature on a rocker.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation and detection
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with HRP‑conjugated secondary antibody diluted 1:5 000 in 5 % milk/TBST for 1 h at room temperature on a rocker; rinse twice with TBST and wash three times with TBST for 10 min each at room temperature; decant TBST and add Luminata HRP reagent, incubate 5 min; image the blot using a G:Box ChemiXX6/XX9 high‑resolution imaging system and export the images as 300 dpi TIFF files for figure preparation.

description: Dysregulation of TGF-β signaling is associated with several inflammatory disorders including intestinal inflammation in animal models and inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) in humans.2,3 The amplitude of TGF-β signaling is tightly regulated by Smad proteins.2,3 While Smad7 limits TGF-β signaling, Smad2 and Smad3 promote TGF-β signaling and prevent tissue inflammation and IBD.2,3 Below, we describe a detailed protocol for the analysis of Smad molecules. The phospho flow cytometry approach we describe can be applied to detect a variety of phospho proteins in other signaling pathways at the cellular level with even a small number of cells as compared to time-consuming traditional approaches requiring higher cell numbers.2,4 Further, these methods can also be applied to a variety of cell lines and primary cells such as peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs).
